Effigy

EF-ih-jee -- from Latin effigies ('an image, likeness'), ex- ('out') + fingere ('to shape, form'). · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Effigy is a sculpture or crude model built to represent a specific person, often burned or destroyed in protest.

Furious about the new toll road, protesters built a straw effigy of the governor and set it ablaze outside the capitol.

Worked Example

Each town in the festival builds its own effigy of the departing winter spirit out of branches and old cloth, then burns it at midnight to welcome spring.

That crude model or figure built to stand in for an actual person or spirit -- especially one meant to be symbolically destroyed -- is exactly what an effigy is.

How Effigy Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

likeness

likeness: a representation that resembles a specific person

dummy

dummy: a full figure built to stand in for a person

Antonyms

original

original: the real, genuine person or thing itself

blank

blank: having no image or representation at all

How Strong Is It? — likeness → effigy → dummy

likeness vs. effigy

likeness vs. effigy: A likeness is weaker than an effigy: a sketch merely resembles someone on paper, while an effigy is a built figure of the person, often raised to be mocked or burned.

dummy vs. effigy

dummy vs. effigy: A dummy goes further than an effigy: an effigy needs only a crude resemblance to stand for its target, while a dummy is a complete, full-bodied model built to take a person's place.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ef-

Prefix — ef-: out (the form ex- takes before f) (Latin)

Root — fig

Root — fig: to shape, form (from Latin fingere -- the same root in figure and fiction)

Suffix — -y

Suffix — -y: noun-forming ending (from Latin -ies, via French)

Put it together

Put it together: Ef- ('out' -- the shape ex- takes before f) + fig ('to shape, form', from Latin fingere) + -y spell effigy: quite literally, a shape formed to stand out as a likeness of someone.

Use the root in a new word: figure

Use the root in a new word: figure: The museum displayed a life-sized wax figure of the explorer beside his original expedition gear.
